entries.title: Gallium Anomaly May Finally Be Explained
entries.summary: Author(s): Ryan Wilkinson A decades-old neutrino mystery might be solved not by undiscovered physics but by improved calculations. [Physics 19, s116] Published Thu Sep 24, 2026

entries.title: A Type-I Superconductor Breaks Time-Reversal Symmetry
entries.summary: Author(s): Rachel Berkowitz A hallmark property of unconventional superconductivity has been discovered in a type-I superconductor, whereas it’s normally observed only in type-II materials. [Physics 19, s115] Published Wed Sep 23, 2026

entries.title: How to Tell If Your Excitons Have Condensed
entries.summary: Author(s): David Ehrenstein A newly predicted effect should provide a clean way to distinguish between a Bose-Einstein condensate of quasiparticles called excitons and a more mundane collection of these particles. [Physics 19, s124] Published Tue Sep 22, 2026

entries.title: The Turbulent Life of a Vortex Line
entries.summary: Author(s): Andrew Baggaley A tabletop experiment using a classical water vortex supports a decades-old theory describing the decay of turbulence in quantum fluids. [Physics 19, 118] Published Mon Sep 21, 2026

entries.title: Collimating Positrons with Superconducting Magnets
entries.summary: Author(s): Sam Jarman A recent experiment points the way toward making the intense, energetic beams of positrons needed for next-generation electron–positron colliders. [Physics 19, 127] Published Fri Sep 18, 2026

entries.title: A laser that stays locked without active control
entries.summary: EPFL researchers have developed a chip-based laser that keeps a very stable frequency across its tested operating range, without needing active electronic control. Their research is published in the journal Nature Photonics.
